series.lore: For the third time in a few days, the Seekers have reported warm winds rising from the plains. But “Spring” is now only a borrowed word: the cycle of seasons the Celestial Dragon once kept is long lost, and only a misshapen echo remains. In recent weeks I have charted the movements of many creatures, and I no longer have any doubt: they are abandoning their territories. Predators of the peaks descend into the marshes; beasts of the forest venture underground or into the dunes, as if this warm wind were calling them to seek something. A party of hunters has just set out on a long expedition. They will be gone for at least five weeks, and will face those creatures far from their lairs. I watch them depart, and I find myself wondering whether this spring is at work in us as well. Something blooms within us that we do not remember planting.
series.name: Winds of Spring

series.lore: The heat has dried the roots and drained the rivers. Since we founded Alborea, this is the first year the city has gone hungry. The forests here have always given us food in plenty, but this year the wind of summer has come to weigh on the land like the shadow of a dragon. In my hands is the ancient codex I found sealed in a tomb. I turn its pages to the Rite of Summer. The ancients said they had made a pact with Thyrea, and that each year, before summer, they renewed their promise. At winter’s end the whole clan came together and chose its strongest warrior, the one whose hunting had fed them. The warrior stepped forward and offered to give up that strength to Thyrea, for the promise of a summer of plenty. Then a priestess struck the warrior with a gilded dagger and laid the body out in the middle of a clearing, where Thyrea would drink the blood. All through the night the body lay still: the stars too had to see. At dawn the warrior rose, and the whole clan celebrated. They were in harmony with Thyrea again. I close the codex. Perhaps the pact still holds. For years Thyrea has waited on us for a sacrifice, and now the price is higher: when we take the heart of the monster we have killed, we will know it must be offered to the earth, which thirsts and hungers.
series.name: Winds of Summer
